facts.raw_span: A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Antrum: normal appearance
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
Three defined layers: first (foveolar epithelium) showed foveolar hyperplasia
second (parietal cells) was shortened with mild degeneration
H+/K+-ATPase staining: heterogeneously reduced
Anti-parietal cell antibody: <1:10 (negative)
Serum gastrin: 150 pg/mL (normal 37–172)
Anti-H. pylori IgG: <3 U/mL (negative)
A 37-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus and Sjögren’s syndrome
was diagnosed with autoimmune hepatitis
Vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable
Antrum: normal appearance
Gastric corpus: normal coloration with a regular arrangement of collecting venules; red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle
Magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus: regular round pit patterns
Three defined layers: first (foveolar epithelium) showed foveolar hyperplasia
second (parietal cells) was shortened with mild degeneration
H+/K+-ATPase staining: heterogeneously reduced
Anti-parietal cell antibody: <1:10 (negative)
Serum gastrin: 150 pg/mL (normal 37–172)
Anti-H. pylori IgG: <3 U/mL (negative)

concepts.why: The patient's histologic findings, including foveolar hyperplasia, shortened parietal cells with mild degeneration, and heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining, are consistent with autoimmune gastritis.

The patient's endoscopic and histologic findings, including red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle, foveolar hyperplasia, and shortened parietal cells with mild degeneration, are consistent with chronic gastritis.

The patient's histologic findings, including foveolar hyperplasia, shortened parietal cells with mild degeneration, and heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining, are consistent with gastric mucosal atrophy.

Although the patient's vitamin B12 level is within the normal range, the presence of autoimmune hepatitis and Sjögren's syndrome, as well as the negative anti-parietal cell antibody and anti-intrinsic factor antibody, suggest a possible risk for pernicious anemia.
The regular round pit patterns on magnified narrow-band imaging of the corpus explain the uncovered finding of inflammation in the gastric corpus.

rationales.F05: Red streaks and mucosal swelling suggest inflammation, which is more typical of gastric corpus inflammation.
rationales.F08: Shortened parietal cells with mild degeneration are characteristic of autoimmune gastritis.
rationales.F09: Heterogeneously reduced H+/K+-ATPase staining is indicative of autoimmune gastritis.
rationales.F10: Negative anti-parietal cell antibody makes autoimmune gastritis less likely.
rationales.F12: Negative Anti-H. pylori IgG reduces the likelihood of chronic gastritis and gastric mucosal atrophy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The endoscopic findings of red streaks and slight mucosal swelling on the lesser curvature of the angle, along with the histologic findings of foveolar hyperplasia, mild degeneration of parietal cells, and mild lymphocytic infiltration, support the diagnosis of chronic gastritis.
